item.text: I’ll use the Deep Research Council skill to check the headline against the two reports in the packet.

**Corrected headline**  
District literacy among residents aged 15 or older was estimated at 84% in 2025, up from an estimated 82% in 2024, while 91% of program participants who took the 2025 reading test passed (`statistics-report.md`, §3 “Population estimate”; `education-report.md`, §4 “Completion assessment”).

**The official figures are compatible.** The household survey estimates the share of all district residents aged 15 or older who can read a short everyday passage. The program counted 273 passes among 300 voluntarily enrolled adults who completed its assessment. Subtracting the 2024 survey estimate from the 2025 program pass rate produces the draft’s nine-point figure, but that calculation compares different groups and measures (`draft-headline.md`, §1; `statistics-report.md`, §3; `education-report.md`, §4).

**What remains unresolved.** The survey used the same sampling frame and field method in both years, so its point estimates support a **two-percentage-point increase in estimated literacy**. The 95% intervals were 79–85% in 2024 and 81–87% in 2025. Their overlap alone cannot settle whether population literacy actually rose, and the report gives no formal test of the change. The program report has no control group, and neither report estimates the campaign’s effect. Its contribution remains unknown (`statistics-report.md`, §3; `education-report.md`, §4).
